name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans roughly 28 points Republican, among the reddest seats on the ballot
Incumbent Josh Brecheen has a massive money edge: about $219,000 raised versus $4,300 for Brandon Wade, who has $86 on hand
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at roughly 1 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; independent Ronnie Hopkins is also on the ballot
model.rationale: A 28-point Republican lean, a sitting incumbent, and a challenger with essentially no campaign leave no plausible Democratic path; betting markets and the lopsided fundraising gap both point to a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen scandal or a late wave of outside spending against Brecheen could put the outcome in doubt; absent that, the race stays safely Republican.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 2nd District sits deep in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 28 points toward the GOP. Republican incumbent Josh Brecheen is seeking re-election and holds every structural advantage: he has raised about $219,000 and reported $76,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Brandon Wade has raised roughly $4,300 and has just $86 in the bank. No outside groups are spending in the race, and an independent candidate, Ronnie Hopkins, is also on the ballot without visible fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the lopsided money picture. Betting markets give the Democrat about a 1 percent chance of winning. Everything points to a comfortable Republican hold, with the real question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
